title: Both Bishops
setup: White is a rook and a knight down, the black king never castled, and both white bishops are pointing at it.
hint: Count the black king's squares before you count material — what is left once the bishop on a3 and the pawn on f6 are subtracted?
explanation:
## The Idea

{{Qxd7+}} throws the queen at a defended pawn. Declining with {{Kf8}} is mate at once on e7, so {{Kxd7}}, and the king stands in the open with both bishops aimed at it.

{{Bf5+}} is double check, from the bishop and from the rook behind it. {{Kc6}} walks into {{Bd7#}}, and after {{Ke8}}, {{Bd7+}} and {{Bxe7#}} finish it with the same two bishops.

Anderssen played this in Berlin in 1852, a year after the Immortal Game.
